chunks: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose brother sent his zakat to him to distribute it, but it got wasted. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon the messenger, nor upon the payer, any responsibility.' I said, 'So if he does not find a deserving one for it, and it gets spoilt, and altered, would he be responsible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if he recognised a deserving one for it, so it got damaged, or spoilt, so he would be responsible for it until he extracts it'.
ai.seo_question: When is a messenger liable for lost zakat funds?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the principle of conditional liability (daman) for zakat distributors, distinguishing between loss due to unavoidable circumstances when recipients are unknown, and negligence when recipients are identified. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the messenger's duty to actively seek out the deserving poor (mustahiqqeen) rather than merely holding the funds, ensuring the religious obligation is fulfilled effectively.
